clue.text: Sodium chloride in tree top

indicators.note: in places the formula for the salt inside the tree, which then wraps round it

parts.note: NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt

explanation.surface: Salt has been found at the top of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is the highest point or peak of something, so a synonym for top.

clue.text: A giant in a state of eager desire

definitions.text: in a state of eager desire

parts.note: Gog is one of the legendary giants Gog and Magog, guardians of the City of London

explanation.surface: A huge person who is keen and eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant, wide-eyed with excitement.

clue.text: A proper American stove?

parts.note: US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: Asking whether a decent stove would be an American one.
explanation.walkthrough: The Primus is a portable paraffin stove, used by campers; the question mark flags the brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: Primus is a well-known make of portable camping stove, so it is a stove by example.

clue.text: Lords and ladies agree to differ in the outskirts of Prague

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the two edge letters
the outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters of the city are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the city name

indicators.note: differing means becoming different, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: Aristocrats on the edge of Prague settle a dispute by agreeing to differ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lords and ladies' is also a wild plant name, a tempting false lead.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the body of peers: titled lords and ladies collectively.

clue.text: Little flowers cultivated in beds. Ours?

indicators.note: cultivated means worked over like turned soil, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener asks whether the small flowers growing in the beds are theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosebuds are unopened roses, small flowers yet to bloom.

clue.text: Always a great news paper

parts.note: great in the sense of large or high
The Times, the London daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A boast that some newspaper is always a great one.
explanation.walkthrough: Splitting 'news paper' into two words hints at a title rather than any old paper.
explanation.definitionFit: At all times is an idiom meaning on every occasion, so a synonym for always.

clue.text: When uprising and revolution reveal a god

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the little word is turned around

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A rebellion and a revolution expose a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising and revolution' reads as a political pair, but the first word works on 'When' and the second is a simple synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the Roman god of agriculture and time, so a god by example.

clue.text: Heather Lake's dress

definitions.note: lingerie is underclothing, so 'dress' is meant in its broad sense of clothing

parts.note: ling is the common heather plant
Lake Erie, one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather Lake and the outfit she is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather Lake reads as a person's name; split it into a plant and a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear, a category of clothing or dress in the general sense of garments worn.

clue.text: Expenditure dismissed with a song

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
a lay is a short song or ballad

explanation.surface: Spending was cut, and somebody sang about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is the money laid out, a synonym for spending or expenditure.

clue.text: Weapons put back in the bar-parlour

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the opposite way, so the word for weapons is written in reverse order

explanation.surface: Someone tucks the weapons away in the pub's back room.
explanation.walkthrough: A snug is a small cosy room in a British pub, a bar-parlour.
explanation.definitionFit: In British pubs the snug is the small private room, also called the bar-parlour.

clue.text: A poet gets so upset about uranium. That's astonishing

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the short word is turned round and read the other way
about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round the symbol for the element

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A poet is distraught over uranium, which is surprising news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A poet' must be a particular one: Andrew Marvell. Turn SO round to OS and put U inside it to finish the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marvellous excites wonder, so it is a near synonym for astonishing.

clue.text: Players or cast, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters are only one possible arrangement, inviting a rearranging

explanation.surface: Players, or the cast of a show: a list of near synonyms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a second definition, but it is part of the letters to rearrange, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors are players in a theatre, and together they form the cast of a production.

clue.text: Poor art's seldom produced by great artists

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the letters are in a bad order and must be fixed

explanation.surface: Great painters rarely turn out bad work.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Masters are the great European painters from before about 1800, and their works.

clue.text: Those who eat to excess produce too much weight

parts.note: to glut a market is to oversupply it

explanation.surface: Overeaters end up producing excess body weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about getting fat; split it into a definition, a verb and a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A glutton is a person who habitually eats far more than needed.

clue.text: People on slopes in the hills

explanation.surface: Skiers or walkers on the slopes up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mendips are a range of limestone hills in Somerset, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mendip Hills are a named range in Somerset, so 'the hills' is a definition by example.

clue.text: A swan song shows taste

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a chant is a sung melody

explanation.surface: Someone's last work, their swan song, reveals their refined taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swan song' is an idiom for a final performance; split it, and the bird and the song give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a liking or fondness, which is taste in the sense of preference.

clue.text: Ham lies about Abraham's son

indicators.note: about can mean all around or in disorder, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ham, one of Noah's sons, tells lies about another biblical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Ham is also a son in Genesis, which keeps the biblical surface intact.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Ishmael is Abraham's first son, born to Hagar.

clue.text: Trade Union embracing the French revolution and a socialist ideal?

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so the union's name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Equity is the British actors' trade union

indicators.note: a revolution turns something over, so the French article is written backwards

explanation.surface: A union welcomes the French Revolution and its socialist ideals.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the British actors' union. The surface evokes 'liberty, equality, fraternity', the French Revolution's slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: Equality, everyone having equal rights and wealth, is a core aim of socialism; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: A series of steps — about five — to move forwards

indicators.note: about means around, so the steps go round the numeral

parts.note: a dance is a sequence of steps
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A set of about five steps lets you go forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to go forward or progress, so a synonym for move forwards.

clue.text: Got into a bed, dressed

indicators.note: dressed as in prepared or arranged, like dressed stone, so the letters are put into new order

explanation.surface: Someone climbed into bed with their clothes still on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got into a bed' reads as one phrase, but 'Got' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to get it, so the past tense obtained matches got.

clue.text: A tool? The pointed end was turned up!

parts.note: the bow is the pointed front end of a ship

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read upwards, so the little word is written backwards

explanation.surface: Someone finds a tool lying with its sharp end pointing upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pointed end' sounds like part of the tool, but it is a ship's front.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowsaw is a saw with a thin blade stretched across a bow-shaped frame, a woodworking tool.

clue.text: The post office has regrets about an attitudiniser

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for post office

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for regrets is read backwards

explanation.surface: The post office apologises to a pretentious customer.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitudiniser strikes affected attitudes, which is what a poseur does: someone who puts on airs.

clue.text: Pushing a ruler under a river

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means placed below, so the ruler is written after the river rather than before it

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: A monarch is being pushed into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under' places the ruler below the river, so the river comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Poking is prodding or pushing with a finger or stick.

clue.text: Ride in the fairground and revert to the status quo?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a roller-coaster with steep ups and downs
second meaning: to change back, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning splits the answer into a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchback is a fairground roller-coaster, and to switch back is to return to the earlier state.

clue.text: Some malevolent little beast

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the answer is just a section of the next word

parts.note: letters three to six of this word

explanation.surface: A spiteful small creature, perhaps a pest in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A vole is a small rodent, fairly called a little beast or creature.

clue.text: Change course? Move erratically? Not entirely!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to swing to a new direction
second meaning: to swerve, a movement that is only partly erratic

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' hedges the second meaning: to veer is to swerve unsteadily, close to but not quite moving erratically.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer is to swing suddenly to a different direction, both a change of course and a swerving movement.

clue.text: Cord — an odd material

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A length of cord made of some unusual fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Dacron is a trade name for a polyester fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Dacron is a synthetic polyester fabric, so it is a material in the textile sense.

clue.text: Whatever is inside is satisfactory

parts.note: is shortened to 's, as in it's

explanation.surface: Whatever is in the box will be fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as CONTENT'S: 'content is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The contents of a container are whatever is inside it.
